title: Seamless smartphone connectivity, dependable in-car charging and robust online features
description: Customers experience reliable Apple CarPlay/Android Auto connections, a passenger wireless charging solution that actually charges common phones and fits typical cases, dependable in-car Wi‑Fi hotspot performance and voice commands that work accurately for common requests.
acceptance_criterion: Connectivity validation: (a) Wireless Apple CarPlay/Android Auto establishes and maintains a usable connection within 10 seconds in ≥95% of paired attempts in real-world tests; (b) the main wireless charge pad charges common phones at ≥7.5 W (Qi) and successfully charges 95% of tested phone+case combinations while vehicle is in normal driving; (c) vehicle Wi‑Fi maintains a usable internet connection for streaming (3+ Mbps) for ≥90% of 30-minute sessions in suburban test scenarios; (d) voice recognition correctly executes 90% of a 100-command phrasal test representing common navigation/media/climate commands.

reach.explanation: 57 of at most 613 mentions (square root scale); US = 25 % of 2030 volume

competitive_pressure.explanation: no trusted web source shows a competitor advantage

rationale: Ranked mainly because of customer pain (25 points) and satisfaction gap (12.8 points). Evidence level A: 57 mentions, confirmed by 3 independent source types.
assumptions: Wireless CarPlay/Android Auto protocols and smartphone OS behavior will remain compatible with OEM implementations in the successor timeframe.
Wireless charge power targets reference typical Qi charging rates used by phone manufacturers.
uncertainties: Phone model and case interference can still prevent charging; absolute guarantees across every phone are not feasible.
Cellular network variability affects Wi‑Fi hotspot performance beyond OEM control.

offer_check.note: Smartphone Integration is standard; wireless charging (O52), 4G LTE (O34) and Personal eSIM (O51) also included. (Smartphone Integration (Kompatibles Smartphone erforderlich)7)

title: Climate controls and vents must be fast, discoverable and operable without visual attention
description: Customers can quickly find and operate HVAC functions and direct airflow without hunting through menus. Vent outlets and their controls are visible and intuitive, and basic temperature/fan adjustments can be made by feel or a single control while driving.
acceptance_criterion: Usability and safety testing: (a) 90% of participants can locate and adjust fan speed and temperature within 2 seconds without looking at the screen using tactile controls or a dedicated physical interface; (b) vents are visibly and physically adjustable and reachable from driver and front-passenger seats, with ≥90% of users rating vent discoverability as 'easy' in a 50-person test.

reach.explanation: 39 of at most 613 mentions (square root scale); US = 25 % of 2030 volume

satisfaction_gap.explanation: Operation of heater/ AC controls: 15 % unsatisfied

competitive_pressure.explanation: no trusted web source shows a competitor advantage

rationale: Ranked mainly because of customer pain (25 points) and satisfaction gap (12 points). Evidence level A: 39 mentions, confirmed by 2 independent source types.
assumptions: A combination of tactile controls and simplified touchscreen surfaces will be used to meet the requirement.
Ergonomic placement of vents and controls is feasible within packaging constraints.
uncertainties: Some design themes emphasize minimalism which can limit physical control placement; trade-offs may be required.

offer_check.note: Intelligent Personal Assistant provides voice control for climate, enabling hands-free operation without visual attention. (Intelligent Personal Assistant6)

title: Default door-unlock behavior should match customer expectations and be easy to change
description: When customers approach the vehicle with authorized access, doors unlock in an obvious, expected way (defaulting to unlocking all passenger doors), and the setting to change behavior is easy to find and persists across key cycles.
acceptance_criterion: Field and usability validation: (a) Default out-of-the-box behavior unlocks all doors on approach for the primary key and is documented in the quick-start guide; (b) changing the unlock behavior is achievable within two menu steps or one dedicated UI element, and 95% of a 100-owner panel successfully change and persist the setting; (c) ≤3% of owners report unexpected single-door-only unlock events in a 90‑day ownership study.

reach.explanation: 28 of at most 613 mentions (square root scale); US = 25 % of 2030 volume

competitive_pressure.explanation: competitor advantage backed by a high-trust web source

rationale: Ranked mainly because of customer pain (24.1 points) and competitive pressure (15 points). Evidence level B: 28 mentions, confirmed only by web sources: A needs a second BMW source (study).
assumptions: Default choices can be set at production and exposed via a short, discoverable setting in the infotainment or physical controls.
User education (quick-start guide, first-use prompts) will be used to surface behavior.
uncertainties: Regional security preferences may lead some owners to prefer different defaults; offering a clear setting mitigates this.

offer_check.note: Contains Komfortzugang and Travel & Comfort System, providing keyless access and menu settings to adjust default unlock behavior. (TRAVEL PAKET)

title: Provide a clear, efficient operating concept for the touchscreen: fewer taps, better discoverability, and accessible odometer/trip info
description: Customers can complete common tasks quickly without confusion or menu hunting: climate and core vehicle functions are easy to access, the odometer/trip mileage is clearly visible via the instrument cluster or two quick taps, and the large display remains elegant without overwhelming menus or excessive smudging.
acceptance_criterion: Human factors testing: (a) 95% of participants complete six core tasks (set cabin temperature, change fan speed, switch drive mode, access odometer/trip, start navigation to home, pair phone) within ≤5 seconds and ≤3 interactions/taps, without looking away from the road for more than 2 seconds; (b) odometer/trip mileage is reachable within ≤2 taps from the primary instrument cluster view; (c) perceived clutter rating ≤15% dissatisfied in a 100‑person usability study and touchscreen legibility in direct sunlight achieves a measured contrast ratio consistent with readability standards.

customer_pain.explanation: Mostly complaints (Difficult to Use / Wants), 115 mentions

reach.explanation: 115 of at most 613 mentions (square root scale); US = 25 % of 2030 volume

satisfaction_gap.explanation: Menu structure of infotainment system: 13 % unsatisfied

competitive_pressure.explanation: no trusted web source shows a competitor advantage

rationale: Ranked mainly because of customer pain (19.5 points) and satisfaction gap (10.4 points). Evidence level A: 115 mentions, confirmed by 2 independent source types.
assumptions: UI redesign and HMI changes can reduce menu depth and expose key functions as user-customizable shortcuts.
Display hardware improvements (anti-reflective coatings) and software theming can materially improve sunlight legibility.
uncertainties: Conflicting evidence: "Love the large touchscreen and long display" vs. "Too many menus and the screen gets dirty"
Some drivers will continue to prefer deeper customization even if core tasks are simplified.
Hardware constraints (e.g., bezel, sensor placement) may limit some legibility improvements.

offer_check.note: BMW Operating System 8.5 provides the touchscreen user interface and menu structure aiming for intuitive navigation and instrument information access. (BMW Operating System 8.5)

title: Improve interior storage and phone tray design so items fit securely and storage is practical
description: Customers find storage compartments that are well-placed, sized for modern items (phones with cases, wallets, sunglasses), and a wireless phone tray that keeps phones stable and charges reliably. Overall cabin storage is intuitive and reduces clutter.
acceptance_criterion: User validation: (a) 95% of tested phone+case combinations sit flat and remain stable on the primary tray during standardized lane-change maneuvers; (b) a cabin storage usability survey shows ≥85% of participants rate general storage capacity/placement as 'sufficient' or 'good'; (c) no more than 5% of owners report a wireless tray that fails to hold or charge their phone in initial 30‑day use.

customer_pain.explanation: Mostly complaints (Difficult to Use / Defect), 27 mentions

reach.explanation: 27 of at most 613 mentions (square root scale); US = 25 % of 2030 volume

competitive_pressure.explanation: no trusted web source shows a competitor advantage

rationale: Ranked mainly because of customer pain (25 points) and satisfaction gap (8 points). Evidence level A: 27 mentions, confirmed by 2 independent source types.
assumptions: Phone sizes and typical cases continue to follow current trends; major new form factors could require later adjustment.
Physical retention features (lip, textured surface) are acceptable to customers versus a strictly flat tray.
uncertainties: Very large phones or non-standard cases may still require a cable; impossible to guarantee fit for every accessory.

offer_check.note: Wireless Charging Ablage provides a dedicated, secure phone tray improving phone fit and practical storage. (Wireless Charging Ablage)

title: Realistic and stable EV range estimates and improved charging speed guidance
description: Customers see a consistent, trustworthy displayed electric range that closely matches real-world consumption across common usage and conditions, and receive clear guidance about charging compatibility and expected times so they can plan trips without repeated range anxiety. The vehicle supports widely used public charging standards or adapters and provides preconditioning guidance when needed.
acceptance_criterion: Range and charging validation: (a) Worldwide on-road testing across warm and cold conditions shows the displayed remaining electric range is within ±10% of measured real-world range in 90% of trips over 50 miles; (b) at common DC public chargers (150 kW class), the vehicle charges to 80% state-of-charge in ≤30 minutes when ambient/pack conditions allow (measured in standardized test); (c) navigation/charging UI lists compatibility and nearby available stations with real-time status and success guidance, and user tests show 90% of participants can find a compatible nearby charger within 60 seconds.

reach.explanation: 120 of at most 613 mentions (square root scale); US = 25 % of 2030 volume

competitive_pressure.explanation: competitor advantage backed by a high-trust web source

future_relevance.explanation: rests partly on a forward-looking assumption

rationale: Ranked mainly because of customer pain (20.6 points) and competitive pressure (15 points). Evidence level B: 120 mentions, confirmed only by web sources: A needs a second BMW source (study).
assumptions: Public charging networks and station power levels will continue to improve; successor vehicle battery and thermal management enable faster charging within safe limits.
Charging time targets assume a sufficiently powerful charger is available (e.g., ≥150 kW).
uncertainties: Conflicting evidence: "Range feels limited and fluctuates" vs. "Range is better than quoted and fits commute"
Actual achieved charging speeds depend on public charger power, queuing, and network availability.
Range accuracy can be affected by driver behavior, payload, terrain and weather; precise calibration across all conditions is challenging.

offer_check.note: No listed option provides EV range prediction or charging speed guidance; only charging hardware and general connectivity are present.

title: Braking should feel confident and quiet with low dust and no grabby behavior
description: Customers experience brakes that stop smoothly and quietly without squeal or grinding, produce noticeably less visible rotor/pad dust on wheels, and deliver a consistent, progressive pedal feel that does not feel grabby or cause jerky stops.
acceptance_criterion: In durability and NVH testing and early-owner validation: (a) ≤2% of a 200-owner initial ownership cohort report brake squeal/grinding within first 3 months; (b) measured wheel-dust mass after a standardized urban driving loop is reduced by ≥30% versus the G60 baseline; (c) subjective pedal feel 'grabby' rating ≤10% negative in a 50-driver braking perception panel.

reach.explanation: 32 of at most 613 mentions (square root scale); US = 25 % of 2030 volume

competitive_pressure.explanation: competitor advantage backed by a high-trust web source

rationale: Ranked mainly because of customer pain (23 points) and competitive pressure (15 points). Evidence level B: 32 mentions, confirmed only by web sources: A needs a second BMW source (study).
assumptions: Improved friction material and brake system calibration can reduce dust and NVH without unacceptable trade-offs in stopping distance.
G60 baseline dust measurements are available for comparison.
uncertainties: Brake dust and NVH depend on wheel finish, contaminant exposure and driver style; variation across markets may occur.
Perception thresholds for 'squeal' differ between users.

offer_check.note: No offered option specifies quiet, low-dust, non-grabby braking; only an M Sport brake is listed.

acceptance_criterion: Documentation and equipment validation: (a) Each vehicle is delivered with either a run-flat tire solution or an inflator/repair kit and clear owner instructions; (b) in a representative owner survey, dissatisfaction related to flat tire preparedness falls to ≤10% (from current 18% study baseline); (c) emergency tire information and repair instructions are discoverable in ≤2 taps from the main vehicle info screen and in the quick-start guide.

title: Keep the BMW driving character: strong, smooth and predictable acceleration with controllable sportiness
description: Customers experience strong, repeatable acceleration and a refined, planted ride: the car still feels quick and sporty when demanded, yet smooth, linear and predictable across everyday driving and mode changes. Sporty launch and responsive throttle are available without abrupt surges, jerks or late/harsh transitions between electric and combustion assistance, and drivers can choose driveline feel through My Modes.
acceptance_criterion: In instrumented vehicle validation and owner trials: (a) 0–60 mph is within ±5% of the advertised value for the tested trim on 95% of runs; (b) driver-perceived abrupt torque spikes or jerk events occur in ≤5% of logged throttle transitions across 1,000 real-world test miles; (c) in a 30‑driver user panel, ≥90% rate acceleration as 'smooth and appropriately strong' in both Comfort and Sport/My Modes.
